items.text: A mason is building a below-grade masonry retaining wall in earth contact. Which mortar type is specified?
B. Type M — Per ASTM C270, Type M (2,500 psi) is the mortar for below-grade work, foundations, retaining walls, and earth contact; Type N is the general above-grade veneer mortar.
What is the minimum compressive strength of Type S mortar?
C. 1,800 psi — ASTM C270 sets Type S at 1,800 psi minimum - the structural at-or-above-grade mortar with the best lateral strength; 2,500 is Type M and 750 is Type N.
What is the minimum compressive strength of masonry grout?
A. 2,000 psi — ASTM C476 requires grout to reach a minimum of 2,000 psi; it is a fluid mix poured into CMU cells around rebar, unlike mortar which goes in bed and head joints.
Below what temperature may masonry NOT be laid without a heated enclosure?

D. 20 degrees Fahrenheit — Cold-weather masonry practice prohibits laying below 20 degrees F without a heated enclosure; below 40 degrees F the water and sand are heated and the work is protected 24 hours, and antifreeze is never added.
A brick wall shows white powdery deposits. What is the correct fix?

C. Correct the water path with flashing and weeps - the deposit is efflorescence left by migrating water — Efflorescence is the salt deposit left when water migrates through masonry and evaporates - the corpus rule is fix the water (flashing, weeps), not the stain.
What air space is required between brick veneer and the sheathing?
A. Minimum 1 inch, maximum 4 and one-half inches — R703.8.4 requires a 1-inch minimum and 4-1/2-inch maximum air space between veneer and sheathing; 2 inches is the chimney clearance trap.
What are the minimum requirements for a corrugated sheet-metal veneer tie?
B. No. 22 gage and seven-eighths inch wide — R703.8.4.1 requires corrugated sheet-metal ties of at least No. 22 gage and 7/8 inch width, each supporting no more than 2.67 square feet.
A steel lintel supports brick veneer over a window. What minimum bearing is required at each end?
D. 4 inches — R703.8.3 requires lintels supporting veneer to bear a minimum of 4 inches at each end; a typical 3 by 3 by one-quarter inch steel angle spans up to 6 feet.
How must a water-resistive barrier of No. 15 felt be lapped?

B. At least 2 inches at horizontal laps and 6 inches at vertical laps, upper over lower — R703.2 requires WRB horizontal laps of at least 2 inches and vertical laps of at least 6 inches, installed shingle-fashion with upper layers over lower - reversing the two numbers is the listed trap.
Bricks are set on end with their narrow face out in a course above a window opening. What is this course called?
A. Soldier course — A soldier course is brick on end with the face out, typically used over openings; rowlock is on the face edge for sills and caps, and sailor is on end with the broad face out.
Which statement about masonry movement joints is correct?

C. Concrete block shrinks, so CMU walls get control joints, while clay brick expands and gets expansion joints — The corpus rule is opposite behavior: clay brick expands (expansion joints with compressible filler) while CMU shrinks (control joints as a continuous vertical break), spaced roughly 20 to 25 feet and at openings.
How is horizontal joint reinforcement typically placed in a residential CMU wall of 8-inch block?

D. 9-gage ladder or truss wire in the bed joints every 16 inches vertically - every other course — The corpus specifies 9-gage ladder or truss wire in bed joints every 16 inches vertically, which is every other course of 8-inch block, for crack control.
What wall thickness does R1001.5 require for a masonry firebox?

B. 10 inches of solid masonry, or 8 inches total where lined with firebrick — R1001.5 requires firebox walls of 10 inches solid masonry, or 8 inches total where lined with firebrick, with firebrick joints of one-quarter inch maximum in refractory mortar.
What is the minimum depth of a masonry firebox?
A. 20 inches — R1001.6 requires a minimum firebox depth of 20 inches.
A fireplace opening measures 7 square feet. What hearth extension does R1001.10 require?

C. 20 inches in front and 12 inches on each side — R1001.10 requires a hearth extension of 20 inches front and 12 inches each side where the fireplace opening is 6 square feet or larger; 16 and 8 apply only below 6 square feet.
When may a hearth extension be reduced to three-eighths inch thick?

D. When the firebox opening is raised at least 8 inches above the extension — R1001.9 sets the hearth extension at 2 inches thick minimum, reduced to 3/8 inch where the firebox opening is raised at least 8 inches above the extension; the hearth slab itself is 4 inches.
What clearance to combustibles is required at the BACK face of a masonry fireplace?
A. 4 inches — R1001.11 requires 2 inches of clearance from the front faces and sides but 4 inches from the back face - '2 inches everywhere' is the listed trap.
How high above the top of the fireplace opening must the damper be located?

C. At least 8 inches — R1001.7 requires the damper to be at least 8 inches above the top of the fireplace opening (the lintel), and the lintel itself is noncombustible with 4 inches of bearing each end.
What footing does a masonry chimney or fireplace require?

B. At least 12 inches thick, extending at least 6 inches beyond the face on all sides, below frost depth — R1003.2 requires a footing at least 12 inches thick extending at least 6 inches beyond the face on all sides, founded below frost depth - 42 inches in Michigan.
A fireplace opening measures 36 by 30 inches, which is 1,080 square inches. What minimum area must a ROUND flue have?

D. 90 square inches — R1003.15 sizes a round flue at 1/12 of the fireplace opening area: 1,080 divided by 12 is 90 square inches; 1/10 applies to square flues and 1/8 to rectangular flues with a 2-to-1 or greater aspect ratio.
When is a cricket required behind a chimney?

A. When the chimney dimension parallel to the ridge exceeds 30 inches and the chimney does not intersect the ridge — R1003.20 requires a cricket where the chimney dimension parallel to the ridge is greater than 30 inches and the chimney does not intersect the ridge - 24 and 36 inches are the listed traps.
Which describes a code-compliant chimney crown?

C. Sloped at least 10 degrees, at least 2 inches thick at the outer edge, with a drip overhang projecting at least 2 inches — R1003.9.1 requires the crown sloped at least 10 degrees, at least 2 inches thick at the edge, overhanging at least 2 inches, with the drip edge at least 1-1/2 inches from the chimney face.
Which fastener meets R905.2.5 for asphalt shingles?

B. Galvanized roofing nail, minimum 12-gage shank, three-eighths inch head, penetrating at least three-quarters inch into the sheathing — R905.2.5 requires corrosion-resistant roofing nails with a minimum 12-gage shank and 3/8-inch head, penetrating at least 3/4 inch into the sheathing or through sheathing thinner than 3/4 inch.
What is the code MINIMUM number of fasteners per asphalt strip shingle?

A. 4 per strip shingle — R905.2.6 requires fastening per the manufacturer but never fewer than 4 nails per strip shingle (2 per individual shingle) - 6 nails is a high-wind or manufacturer spec, not the code minimum.
What minimum size is required for step flashing where a shingle roof meets a sidewall?

D. 4 inches high by 4 inches wide — R905.2.8.3 requires sidewall step flashing at least 4 inches high by 4 inches wide, with a kickout diverter at the bottom of the intersection directing water into the gutter.
What minimum width is required for the metal lining of an open valley?
B. 24 inches — R905.2.8.2 requires open valley metal at least 24 inches wide; a roll-roofing valley instead uses an 18-inch bottom ply and a 36-inch top ply.
What is the minimum roof slope for standing seam metal roofing?
C. One-quarter unit vertical in 12 — R905.10.2 allows standing seam metal down to 1/4:12; lapped metal panels without sealant need 3:12 and with sealant 1/2:12.
How far must siding fasteners penetrate under the general rule of R703.3.3?

A. At least one and one-quarter inches into sheathing and framing combined — R703.3.3 requires siding fasteners to penetrate a minimum of 1-1/4 inches into sheathing and framing combined, unless the manufacturer or a test report allows otherwise.
How many coats of exterior plaster are required over metal lath, and how long must each coat be moist-cured?

D. 3 coats, each moist-cured at least 48 hours — R703.7 requires 3 coats of stucco over metal or wire lath (2 coats over masonry or concrete), and R703.7.4 requires moist-curing each coat at least 48 hours.
How high above grade must a stucco weep screed be at the base of a framed wall?

B. At least 4 inches above earth, or 2 inches above a paved surface — R703.7.2.1 requires the weep screed at least 4 inches above the earth or 2 inches above paved surfaces - the 6-inch figure is the fiber-cement manufacturer grade clearance, a trap pair.
